scope-review-areas: Abstract, p.1: the paper states the areas it reviews, in the quoted sentence.
def-representation-learning: Section 1, p.1: 'This paper is about representation learning, i.e., ...' gives the paper's own definition.
scope-focus-deep-learning: Section 1, p.1: the paper says it focuses on deep learning methods, composition of multiple non-linear transformations.
def-distributed-representation: Footnote 8, p.4: the paper defines the term 'Distributed representations' in the footnote.
def-sparse-representation: Footnote 9, p.4: the paper defines 'Sparse representations' (k < N).
def-circuit-depth: Section 3.4, p.4: 'The depth of a circuit is the length of the longest path...' is the paper's own definition.
open-training-criteria-disentangling: Section 3.6, p.5: the authors ask how to translate disentangling into training criteria and say 'This question remains clearly open'. It is a limit on their own proposal. The reader kept result_type 'claim'; it is not a measured result.
no-clear-winner-unsupervised-stacking: Section 4, p.6: after surveying approaches to combine unsupervised-pretrained layers, the authors say 'no clear winner emerges and much work has to be done'. It is a caveat on the coverage of their own survey.
def-deep-autoencoder: Section 4, p.6: the paper defines the overall encoder as the composition of the encoders and the decoder as its 'transpose'.
scope-ica-not-covered: Section 5, p.7: the paper says this review does not cover ICA in any detail due to space constraints.
def-explaining-away: Section 6.1.1, p.7: 'explaining away, i.e., a priori independent causes ...' is the paper's definition, followed by an example.
sparse-coding-laplace-prior: Section 6.1.1, p.8, Eq. 4: the paper writes its own probabilistic model for sparse coding with a Laplace prior, matching an L1 penalty.
def-rbm: Section 6.2, p.9: 'It is defined by restricting the interactions in the Boltzmann energy function, in Eq. 7, to only those between h and x' (U = 0 and V = 0).
def-manifold-hypothesis: Section 8, p.16: 'Its premise is the manifold hypothesis, according to which real-world data ... concentrate in the vicinity of a manifold' states the hypothesis the paper uses.
def-dbm: Section 10.2, p.22: the paper defines the DBM as having multiple hidden layers with odd/even conditional independence, and gives its energy function (Eq. 29).
def-local-receptive-fields-sparse: Section 11.2, p.23: the paper defines the topological locality constraint as a very sparse weight matrix with non-zeros only for local connections.
def-l2-pooling: Section 11.2, p.23: 'for which the pool output is the square root of the possibly weighted sum of squares of filter outputs' defines L2 pooling.
def-temporal-coherence-prior: Section 11.3, p.24: the paper gives its own expression for the temporal coherence prior, the squared difference between feature values at t and t+1.
conclusion-three-approaches: Section 12, p.25: the conclusion states the three approaches the review covered.
conclusion-optimization-open: Section 12, p.26: the authors pose the local-minima versus ill-conditioning questions and say they 'remain unanswered and deserve much more study'. It is a stated limit of their discussion of optimization. The reader kept result_type 'claim'.

theory_low.one-hot-parameter-count: Section 3.3, p.4: a 'simple counting argument' stated without proof; the exponential gain is referred to Bengio (2009) and Bengio and Delalleau (2011). Not a proved result.
theory_low.distributed-parameter-count: Section 3.3, p.4: the O(2^k) regions from O(N) parameters is stated, not proved here; the paper points to Bengio (2009) section 3.2. Not a proved result.
theory_low.deep-circuit-paths-exponential: Section 3.4, p.4: stated without proof and supported by cited results (Hastad 1986, Hastad and Goldmann 1991, Bengio and Delalleau 2011). Not proved in this paper.
theory_low.depth-definition-constant-factor: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Section 3.4, p.4 says 'Formally, one can change the depth ... only by a constant factor' with no proof.
theory_low.fewer-parameters-fewer-examples: Section 3.4, pp.4-5: 'learning theory would suggest' is a hedged appeal to learning theory, not a result the paper proves.
theory_low.pca-linear-features-limited: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Section 5, p.7 gives a one-sentence informal argument, that linear maps compose to a linear map. No proof.
theory_low.boltzmann-inference-intractable: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Section 6.2, p.9 gives a term-count illustration (2^(dh-1) terms, Eq. 11), not a proof of intractability.
theory_low.rbm-conditional-factorizes: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Section 6.2, p.9 states the factorization (Eq. 12) with the formula but gives no derivation.
theory_low.rbm-partition-function-intractable: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Section 6.2, p.10 says the partition function still sums exponentially many terms (bounded by min{2^dx, 2^dh}) and calls it 'usually' unmanageable. No proof.
theory_low.linear-ae-same-subspace-pca: textbook, stated not proved (F129): Section 7.1, p.14 states that a linear auto-encoder with squared error learns the PCA subspace, with no proof; Bourlard and Kamp (1988) is cited for the sigmoid case.
